o1.biggest_strength: It follows the money: comparison pages and core product pages get the work, general blog traffic gets cut, and the trial-rate math is clear.
o1.biggest_mistake: It knows the cookie-banner and cookie-free pages are cheap wins, but still waits until Month 2 for /privacy-focused-web-analytics and spends Month 1 on two new comparison pages first.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Move the cookie-banner rewrite and cookie-free retitle into Week 1, before new pages, and make the 90-day forecast more conservative by separating likely gains from best-case ceilings.

o2.biggest_strength: It is disciplined and usable: 12 writer slots, 3 developer days, clear owners, realistic ranges, and a plain first-week plan the team could start on Monday.
o2.biggest_mistake: It underplays the cookie-banner and cookie-free opportunities, and the advice to leave old blog posts unchanged misses the chance to consolidate weak posts into pages that convert.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Put the cookie-banner post and /privacy-focused-web-analytics into Week 1, add a small consolidation plan for decaying blog posts, and keep the same conservative forecasting.

reason: I would rather use Output 2 because it feels more operational and less overconfident. Output 1 has a wider set of good ideas, but Output 2 is closer to a plan the team can execute without me translating it.
